children.title: Trump orders review and reversal of Alaska resource restrictions
children.description_short: Trump signs an Alaska resource-development order directing agencies to review or reverse prior restrictions.
children.description_medium: Executive Order 14153, issued January 20, 2025, set a policy of maximizing natural-resource development on federal and state lands in Alaska. It directed agencies to expedite permitting and leasing and to review or reverse specified prior actions affecting ANWR, the National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska and the Ambler Road project. The order set agency work in motion; it does not establish that 16 million acres became immediately available that day.
children.description_long: Executive Order 14153, “Unleashing Alaska’s Extraordinary Resource Potential,” was issued on January 20, 2025. It set a federal policy of maximizing development on state and federal lands and instructed agencies to expedite permitting and leasing. Its specific directions included rescinding or reviewing earlier actions involving the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, the National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska and the Ambler Road project. The order therefore changed the federal policy direction and required agency action across multiple Alaska resource programs. Its text does not establish that 16 million acres were immediately opened for leasing on January 20. Several of the cited measures were instructions to review, reverse or resume agency processes, rather than proof that later leases or construction had already occurred. The subsequent NPR-A draft analysis and the separate Ambler Road approval were later actions and are covered in separate records. This entry covers the signed January order and keeps its directives distinct from those later agency decisions.

children.title: Interior proposes reopening up to 82% of the National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska
children.description_short: Interior releases a draft analysis supporting a proposed leasing alternative for NPR-A.
children.description_medium: On June 17, 2025, the Department of the Interior released a draft analysis supporting an alternative that would reopen up to 82% of the roughly 23-million-acre National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska to oil and gas leasing and development. The department invited public comment through July 1. This was a proposal in an administrative planning process, not a report that leases had already been issued or development had begun.
children.description_long: On June 17, 2025, the Department of the Interior released a draft analysis for public comment that supported a new alternative in the Bureau of Land Management’s planning process for the National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska. The department said the alternative would reopen up to 82% of the reserve, which it described as 23 million acres, to oil and gas leasing and development. The announcement characterized the measure as a proposal and said the draft analysis would be available for public review. The comment period was scheduled to remain open through July 1, 2025. The release does not say that 82% of the reserve had already been leased or that drilling had started under this alternative. It was a later agency planning step, separate from the January executive order that set the administration’s resource-development policy and from any final management decision or permit. This entry records the proposal as announced and preserves both the stated percentage and its denominator; it does not convert the draft alternative into a completed opening of Alaska acreage.

children.title: Trump approves appeal for proposed Ambler Road and directs permit reissuance
children.description_short: Trump approves AIDEA’s appeal for the proposed 211-mile Ambler Road and directs agencies to reissue permits.
children.description_medium: On October 6, 2025, the White House announced that Trump approved the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority’s appeal concerning the Ambler Road and directed agencies to issue authorizations. The source describes the road as a proposed 211-mile industrial route from the Dalton Highway to the Ambler Mining District. The approval is an administrative step; the source does not say that the road was already built.
children.description_long: On October 6, 2025, the White House announced that President Donald Trump approved the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority’s appeal concerning the Ambler Road Project and directed his administration to issue authorizations. The fact sheet describes the project as a proposed 211-mile industrial road from the Dalton Highway to the remote Ambler Mining District. It says the decision directs the Bureau of Land Management, National Park Service and Army Corps of Engineers to reissue permits needed to construct the road. The announcement is a federal approval and permitting step, not evidence that construction began or that the road opened. It would create road access to a remote mining district, but the source does not establish realized environmental effects. The decision occurred on October 6, months after the January Alaska executive order and after a separate appeal process. It should not be folded into the January order or described as an immediate opening of 16 million acres. This record covers only the later approval and its stated permitting directions.

children.title: Trump declares a national emergency at the southern border
children.description_short: Trump issues Proclamation 10886 declaring a national emergency at the southern border.
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Trump issued Proclamation 10886, declaring a national emergency at the southern border. The proclamation lays out the administration’s stated rationale and directs federal agencies to use specified authorities and resources. It is separate from the March 15 Alien Enemies Act proclamation; the January action itself did not invoke that Act.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump issued Proclamation 10886, “Declaring a National Emergency at the Southern Border of the United States.” The proclamation’s opening presents the administration’s view that the border faced an invasion and describes harms it attributed to unlawful migration, cartels and narcotics. Those are the President’s claims in the proclamation, not independent findings established by the document’s publication. The proclamation directs executive agencies to take actions using specified authorities and resources. It is distinct from the March 15 proclamation that invoked the Alien Enemies Act against Venezuelan nationals the administration alleged were members of Tren de Aragua. The January declaration did not itself invoke that Act. This record captures the emergency declaration and its stated basis without claiming that the declaration began a mass-deportation program, establishing the truth of every factual assertion in its preamble, or adding later enforcement outcomes.

children.title: Trump invokes the Alien Enemies Act against Venezuelans alleged to be Tren de Aragua members
children.description_short: Trump’s March 15 proclamation invokes the Alien Enemies Act and directs removal of people it identifies as alien enemies.
children.description_medium: On March 15, 2025, Trump issued a proclamation invoking the Alien Enemies Act in relation to Tren de Aragua. It asserts that the group was conducting an invasion and declares certain Venezuelan citizens alleged to be members liable to apprehension, detention and removal. These are assertions and commands in the administration’s proclamation, not findings that the allegations against each person are true.
children.description_long: On March 15, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation invoking the Alien Enemies Act in relation to Tren de Aragua. The proclamation asserts that the group was perpetrating or threatening an invasion or predatory incursion and declares certain Venezuelan citizens alleged to be members liable to apprehension, restraint, detention and removal, subject to the criteria it sets out. It directs the Attorney General and the Homeland Security secretary to carry out those measures. The group-membership and invasion statements are the administration’s assertions in the proclamation, not findings by a court that the allegations about each person are true. This action is distinct from the January 20 border emergency proclamation; it occurred nearly two months later and expressly invokes the Alien Enemies Act. This entry describes the issuance and the removal directive without claiming that every person covered was removed or that legal challenges resolved the policy’s validity.
